DESIGN PROTOTYPE
Legal entity federation / Design edition 04

Placement and entitlement are separate problems.

Choose a transport after the ownership, exclusion and physical-boundary rules are explicit.

Option comparison

OptionUseful whenStill required
Native database placementStable residency cohorts within a shared database security/operational boundaryEntity authorization, field projection and lifecycle rules; actual replica/backup placement evidence.
Custom federation — baselineDynamic per-entity/customer sharing and exclusions across independent storesOutbox, OPA enforcement, importer, fences, audit and reconciliation.
Logical data replication — evaluateA supported dedicated projection stream/table matches the selected engine versionSource materialisation, recipient scopes, physical permit checks and revocation semantics.

Current recommendation

Keep the custom source-gated projection path for this thin PoC. Entity placement is a routing and policy input, not a replacement for infrastructure placement controls. Thirty legal entities do not require thirty clusters, but different mandatory physical countries can require additional stores.

No capability assumption

Do not assume a database-native replication feature performs dynamic OPA checks, field filtering or entity-specific revocation. Validate selected-version behaviour and negative paths before replacing the custom transport.

HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Design edition 04: 30 synthetic bank legal entities (UK 3, Asia 8, Americas 3, MENAT 5, rest of Europe 11), mapped independently to three physical PoC stores in Singapore, London and New York. Asia assumes one entity in each of eight countries. All names, mappings and country rules are illustrative, not legal advice or bank policy. Preserve global customer identity; master key is (owner_entity_id, global_customer_id); projection key additionally includes destination_entity_id. Sharing a store or global ID does not share entitlements. OPA evaluates entity grants AND resolved physical country restrictions, with deny override. The downloadable implementation is a single Python/FastAPI harness, three independent CockroachDB single nodes, three OPA engines, outbox polling and OpenTelemetry. The hosted monitor is a labelled browser simulation. Local HA, Java regional services, CDC/Kafka, distributed fencing and signed permits are production extension work. The original v3 catalog planner does not execute migrations. Edition 08 adds an isolated executable relocation slice and optional fourth store; see Entity relocation. Automatic geography failover remains prohibited.

Run a bounded comparison using the same thirty-entity fixtures and negative scenarios. Measure operational cost, isolation, change lifecycle and recovery—not throughput alone. Do not enable any native replication of a full owner table to a disallowed store to test filtering after arrival.
